stats.destruction: 20×2 → 25×2 → 30 }} The Dual Blades are a Medium class melee weapon designed to either deal contact damage or to use its unique ability to ricochet incoming fire in its defensive stance, which also reduces damage taken.   == Usage == The Dual Blades can be selected as the weapon of any Medium build loadout.  The attack trigger can be used to slash opponents in front of the user to damage them. The trigger must be released before attacking again. The attacks will alternate between two quick slashes, from left to right.  The secondary attack trigger can be held down to enter a defensive stance, which can be held for any duration but stops the user from sprinting. During this stance, any incoming bullets or other small projectiles will have their damage to the user greatly reduced if the user is facing in their general direction. Any incoming melee damage is also reduced if the user is facing in the direction of the attacking opponent. If the dual blades user presses mouse 1, they will dash forwards and preform an X slash.  Projectiles that were caught in the defensive stance will be reflected to deal their full damage back to opponents. To control the direction of the reflected projectiles, the user must aim their crosshairs directly at an opponent. The accuracy of these reflected projectiles depends on the accuracy with which they were fired at the user. For example, a reflected bullet from the SR-84 will be very accurate, but a reflected pellet from the SH1900 will not be.  == Stats == *The attack two slashes, each dealing 57 damage.  *Reflected projectiles deal the same damage as the original attack but can't critically hit, even on headshots. Deflecting bullets deals 100% damage to the enemy and 10% to you, or 30% if glancing. *Blocking a melee attack reduces its damage to 25%.  === Properties === ==== Weapon ====  Strikes targets close to the contestant. Can attack forever without reloading.   Attacks once when the trigger is used. The trigger must be released before attacking again, though the next attack can be buffered.   Continues to fire automatically until the trigger is released.   Has a consistent pattern of attacks.   Has an alternate attack that can be held to maintain a defensive stance.    Absorbs part of the damage from enemy attacks and deflects ranged attacks, but does not block explosive damage.   Damages structures. Takes a very long time to break a concrete wall.   Does not critically hit for increased damage, even if the target was struck on the head.  == Guide ==  === Strengths === * The Dual Blades are strong in close-quarters combat. * The Dual Blades' defensive stance can be used while moving towards ann opponent to close the gap. * The Dual Blades' defensive stance offers a significant damage reduction against melee attacks.  === Weaknesses === * The Dual Blades' defensive stance is easily countered if the user is attacked by multiple opponents that are not attacking from the same direction. ** If a Dual Blades user is blocking and walking up to an opponent in one direction, another opponent can assist by going around the Dual Blades user and attacking them from behind. * Explosions and fire are not blocked by the defensive stance.  === Tactics === * To approach an opponent with a ranged weapon, a Dual Blades user can walk up to them while using the defensive stance similarly to the Riot Shield. Once close enough and they stop firing to run away or to reload, the user should switch to the melee attack to deal heavy damage and move quickly. * When facing an SR-84, if the user aims their crosshairs at the sniper rifle user perfectly and deflects a bullet, it is very likely to hit them, dealing full damage.  === Block === *While blocking, incoming fire in front of the user has its damage reduced. More specifically, the vector from the user to the attacker needs to be anywhere between co-directional (0°) and orthogonal (-90° or 90°) to the facing direction of the target.   *If an attack is successfully blocked, it is reduced by 90% if it is a ranged attack, or reduced by 75% if it is a melee attack. **For example, an overhead swing from the Sledgehammer typically deals 175 damage, but will only deal 43.75 damage to a contestant using the Dual Blade's defensive stance.  *The Dual Blades '''cannot''' block the following: RPG, grenade launchers (CL-40 and MGL32), grenades, thrown objects (including canisters), mines, fire/flames, Winch Claw, cannonballs, Orbital Lasers, Meteor Showers, Alien Invasion/Retro Invasion 82.  *The Dual Blades '''can''' block the following: Bullets from Guardian Turret, any melee damage (including the quick melee and Charge 'N' Slam), Throwing Knives, arrows from the Recurve Bow.  === Useful Damage Combinations === {| class="wikitable" !'''Build''' !'''Attack Combo''' !'''Damage''' |- |'''Light''' |'''Primary Fire 1 → Primary Fire 2-1''' |'''<small>50+50+60=</small> 160''' |-

items.imageFile: Mov h spear.gif }} == Usage ==  The Spear can be selected as the weapon of any Heavy build loadout.  The attack trigger can be used to strike opponents in front of the user to damage them. The trigger must be released before attacking again. The first attack will perform a swipe, and the next two attacks, if executed soon enough, will perform a stab attack with increasing damage but a narrow damaging area.  The secondary attack trigger can be used to enter a spinning animation where the user swings their spear in an area of effect, dealing damage three times over 3 seconds. The user can move at 75% of the normal run speed during the animation to control its area.  == Stats == *Primary fire has a range of around 4 meters. *Alternate fire is a 3-hit combo with a slightly shorter range than the primary attack. === Properties === ==== Weapon ====  Strikes targets close to the contestant. Can attack forever without reloading.   Attacks once when the trigger is used. The trigger must be released before attacking again, though the next attack can be buffered.   Has a consistent pattern of attacks. Stabs forwards twice in a narrow area but with increasing damage.   Has an alternate attack which starts a long spinning animation that strikes nearby targets three times.  ==== Attack ====  Damages structures. Takes a very long time to break a concrete wall.  == Guide ==  === Strengths === * The Spear has increased range, with nearly double the attack range of all other melee weapons. * The Spear has an easier time damaging an opponent while chasing them than the comparable Sledgehammer would have, thanks to its increased range and smoother animations. * The Spear's alternate spinning attack is very strong when there are one or multiple opponents in an enclosed area that they cannot easily leave, such as a tight space or the Power Shift platform.  === Weaknesses === * The Spear deals less damage than the comparable Sledgehammer and will often lose an engagement if held in the Sledgehammer's range. It also does not have a way to deal extreme damage in a single attack like the Sledgehammer. * Spin attack doesn't hit very far above and below the player, making it difficult to hit enemies in stairwells and on sloped terrain. * It's easy to accidentally set off mines and C4 with spin attack.  === Tactics === * The Spear can be combined with a Dome Shield, with the user moving in and out of the dome shield while utilizing the Spear's attack range. * The Spear can be combined with a Barricade to great effect. By jumping and attacking with the right timing, the player can hit enemies over the barricade with the primary and secondary attacks. Using a barricade in confined spaces will force enemies to go around it to attack and often give the player a free hit with spin attack. * Smoke can be combined with spin attack to hit enemies without being able to see them. * Winch Claw brings enemies into the Spear's range and allows winch throw to be performed. * Dropping down onto enemies and dropping them onto you is highly effective, especially if they're grouped up within spin attack range. Jump Pad, Zipline, and Gateway are useful for getting the drop on enemies, and RPG, C4, and Dematerializer are useful for dropping enemies.  === Spin Attack === *Each hit deals 75/125/150 damage. *The spin attack animation lasts for 3 seconds, during which it deals damage 3 times. The first hit happens 0.6 seconds in, the second hit happens 1.25 (+0.65) seconds in, and the third hit happens 2.55 (+1.3) seconds in. *Because the third hit comes out much slower than the first two, it's almost always better to emote cancel spin attack after the second hit. See the Tech section for details. *Each hit sweeps in a full circle around the player. The position of the Spear depends on where the player is looking. It's not possible to hit a player more than once with the same sweep. *The hitbox for the spin attack follows the animation to some extent. The Spear first does two turns to the left starting and ending in front of the player. The hitbox is only active for the second turn, hitting in front of the player first and sweeping to the left. The Spear then reverses direction and does one and a quarter turn to the right, again hitting in front of the player first. The third swing reverses again, goes overhead to the left side and does two turns to the left, with an active hitbox for the last turn. *Against single enemies, it's best to face toward them to get damage as early as possible. *Against multiple enemies, it can be advantageous to turn with the attack to increase the effective speed of the Spear and hit enemies earlier. *The player moves at 75% of running speed during the attack. The specialization trigger can be used to perform a dash. The direction of the dash depends on the direction in which its user is attempting to move. For example, if the movement trigger is set to move to the left while activating Evasive Dash, it will perform a dash to the left.  The vertical direction of the dash depends on the looking direction of the user. If the user is looking upwards, the dash will move up. However, Evasive Dash is primarily a horizontal movement tool and cannot go straight up or down.  == Stats == === Effects === Evasive Dash can be activated to dash a short distance, going in a direction based on the user's movement inputs and their looking direction. Uniquely, using this specialization does not interrupt actions such as drawing the Recurve Bow, holding a Sword lunge or scoping in with the SR-84.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be activated to apply an effect to the contestant that used it. items.name: Dematerializer
items.description: A tool that temporarily dematerializes physical surfaces in the arena, allowing any contestant to see or pass through them. It can also make these surfaces rematerialize.
items.descZh: 暂时抹除墙面或天花板物理碰撞，开辟奇袭通道。
items.imageFile: Mov_m_dematerializer.gif }}  == Usage ==  The Dematerializer can be selected as the specialization gadget of any Medium build loadout.  While the gadget is held, looking at a surface will show an indicator of a potential dematerialization as a blue hologram covering a part of the surface. The primary trigger can be used to activate the gadget and dematerialize the surface.   If a surface was already dematerialized by any contestant, the indicator will be red instead, and the secondary trigger can be used to rematerialize the surface.  == Stats == === Effects === The Dematerializer can be deployed by activating it on a targeted surface. This will cause the surface to turn into its dematerialized version. Contestants, attacks and other objects can look and phase through the wall freely. The Dematerializer will remove props attached to wall segments.   After a while, the surface rematerializes automatically, or it can be rematerialized manually.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be activated while targeting a structure piece or solid object.   Can be enabled and disabled by reactivating. Specifically, a dematerialized surface will rematerialize if it is reactivated.   Can be used 2 times. When a charge is used, it automatically recharges over the cooldown time.   Any number of walls can be dematerialized at a time.  ==== Dematerialized Surface ====  Attached to a structure piece or solid object.   Produces a sound to alert nearby contestants when used. A dematerialized surface also hums softly.   Can be used by opponents to their advantage. Opponents can see, shoot and move through the gaps.   Disappears by itself after enough time has passed.   Does not inflict damage.   Instantly removes a surface of any structure. However, this does not affect the structural integrity of the surrounding structure, and the removal is reversed after some time, or upon reactivation.  == Guide == === Strengths === * The Dematerializer can be used to create unexpected angles and opportunities while also being able to close the hole to deny opponents the possibility of retaliation.  === Weaknesses === * If the surfaces around an objective are already breached in several places such as by Explosive Canisters, a Dematerializer user will not get as much benefit from the gadget, as opponents can easily follow them. * It can be difficult to see well through a dematerialized surface to fire through it, due to the glitchy animation overlay, especially if opponents are far away from the surface. * When the user is playing in an uncoordinated team, the Dematerializer may only benefit its user, whereas the other Medium Specializations would also benefit the team. However, with proper communication, the Dematerializer can be used strategically by the entire team. Additionally, capturing objectives using the Dematerializer also benefits the team regardless.  === Tactics === * It is possible to defend an objective from an adjacent room, besides or above the room the station is in, by opening a hole whenever the sound cue plays and taking down the opponent while they are attempting to steal. * To escape from a sticky situation, the user can dematerialize the floor under them or a wall besides them and rematerialize immediately after going through.  ** However, it should be noted that there can sometimes be additional obstacles in unpredictable locations that block the way through, such as a cabinet behind a wall or a pipeline on a ceiling which may require an additional dematerialization. This happens particularly often on Las Vegas and Horizon. * The Dematerializer can be used to take the Cashout Station down a floor and immediately rematerialize the opened ceiling, allowing for a quick steal.  ** Alternatively, if the station is placed against a wall, dematerializing a cell in the wall may allow for an unexpected steal from behind while the rest of the wall and the station itself provides cover for the stealer.  ** These strategies also apply to encrypting or decrypting Terminal Attack's terminal.    ==History== {| class="wikitable" !Patch!!<center>Changes</center> |- |11.6.0|| * Decreased cooldown from 20s to 15s per charge * Decreased item raise time from 0.1s to 0s |- |10.0.0|| * Increased cooldown from 10s to 20s * Increased ammo count from 2 to 3 |- |8.0.0|| *Decreased the number of charges from 3 to 2 *Added new functionality which now remembers exactly which wall segments were dematerialized when a charge was used. *Added a vignette to the screen that will be displayed when a wall segment is dematerialized near the player. *Updated dematerialization visual effect. |- |5.8.0|| *Decreased the duration of dematerialized objects from 30s to 15s, causing objects to rematerialize sooner *Added the ability for the Dematerializer to remove props attached to wall segments  |- |4.0.0|| *Improved targeting to reduce the amount of times the dematerializer fails to make a passageway through objects. |- |2.1.0|| *Improved the dematerializer ability to dematerialize/rematerialized objects when multiple objects are close to each other. |- |}

items.name: Guardian Turret
items.description: Deployable AI-controlled assault rifle
items.descZh: 部署全自动防守炮塔，自动搜寻射击进入范围的敌人。
items.imageFile: Mov_m_guardianturret.gif }}  == Usage ==  The Guardian Turret can be selected as the specialization gadget of any Medium build loadout.  While the gadget is held, an indicator will show a potential placement of the Guardian Turret as a blue hologram in front of the user. If the hologram is red, the gadget will not fit in the target location. The secondary trigger can be used to rotate the placement hologram by 90 degrees. Using the primary trigger, the placement can be confirmed to deploy the gadget. It can be deployed on any surface, including walls and ceilings.  While a Guardian Turret is deployed, the gadget will not start restoring its next charge. The turret must be removed first. If the turret is destroyed, the full cooldown is applied. The gadget can also be retrieved to restore most of its charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.  The Guardian Turret also has a unique remote retrieval option. By holding the secondary trigger on the gadget while a Guardian Turret is deployed, the deployed gadget will be removed, and half of its charge will be refunded.  == Stats == === Effects === The Guardian Turret can be deployed by placing it down on any nearby surface. It arms itself over 5 seconds, after which it starts rotating left and right repeatedly, scanning a total vision cone of 150° (close to half of a circle). The middle of this vision cone is at the orientation of its placement. The vision of the turret has a limited range of about 20m.  Whenever an opponent enters the vision range of the Guardian Turret, it starts firing an unending stream of bullets at them and tracks their movements in the process. Additionally, if an opponent attacks the Guardian Turret, it will turn around to attack them even if they are outside of its vision cone.  The gadget can be damaged only by opponents. Picking up the gadget and placing it again is the only way to restore its health. When the gadget is picked up, a 3s cooldown begins before the turret can be placed again. The gadget has its own visible health bar. Uniquely, the next charge of the gadget will not begin charging until the previous turret is removed.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be placed attached to a surface. An indicator shows the exact target placement.   Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time.   Can be picked up after being deployed. For the Guardian Turret, this does not restore a full charge, but refunds most of the cooldown instead.   Can be commanded to self-destruct by the user from any distance. This refunds half of the cooldown.   Can only be deployed if there is no existing Guardian Turret.  ==== Bullet ====  Travels in a straight line, meaning there is no bullet drop. The direction will deviate from the crosshairs depending on accuracy.   The projectile deals damage if it hits a contestant.   Does not critically hit for increased damage, even if the target was struck on the head.    Can not be removed by the APS Turret.   Does not deal reduced damage when hitting targets at long distances.  ==== Turret ====  Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any carriable object it is attached to.   Has its own collision, meaning it blocks bullets and contestants can stand on it.   Disarmed when initially deployed. Does not detect enemies while disarmed. Arms automatically after a wind-up time. Uniquely, the Guardian Turret remains armed when picked up as an attachment.   Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Has a health bar and cannot take damage from the user's team.   Can be temporarily disabled by a Glitch Grenade or Glitch Barrel.   Can be reshaped by the Data Reshaper into a piece of decor by opponents.   Remains silent while idling, but produces a loud sound on startup and when it locks onto a target, alerting nearby contestants.   Does not disappear by itself.   Cannot be used to damage structures.   Can damage neither the user nor their teammates.  == Guide == === Strengths === * The Guardian Turret can be used to lock down an area. If an opponent enters its line of sight, it will make the team aware an opponent is there thanks to its sound cue.  === Weaknesses === * The Guardian Turret can be disabled by a nearby Glitch Grenade or Glitch Barrel triggering, or reshaped by the Data Reshaper. * The Guardian Turret can be stopped from detecting contestants by disrupting its direct line of sight. Deploying Goo, setting up Barricades, or using Smoke Grenades and Powder Canisters are effective ways to block its vision.  === Tactics === * Placing the Guardian Turret on the ceiling is often a better idea than on the ground, as it won't be harmed by damage from sources such as the Frag Grenade, and melee weapon users will have a hard time dealing with it. Meanwhile, being on the ceiling has little downsides for the Guardian Turret.     == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!<center>Changes</center> |- |10.6.0 || *Increased the vertical vision angle from +-45 degrees to +-60 degrees, making it easier for the turret to attack targets above and below itself |- |10.0.0 || *Increased patrol rotation speed from 30 degrees per second to 40 degrees per second *Decreased turret vision angle from 45 degrees to 40 degrees *Increased damage from 5 to 6 *Decreased fire rate from 450 RPM to 400 RPM *Decreased setup wait time from 4s to 3.5s |- |8.0.0 || * Decreased the cooldown from 40s to 35s * Decreased the cooldown when retrieving the turret from 20s to 17.5s |- |5.8.0 || * Decreased the cooldown from 8s to 3s when manually picking up the Guardian Turret |- |4.0.0 || * Bullets can now be blocked by the player who owns the turret, just like they can be by friendly players |- |3.0.0 || * The cooldown regeneration on the Guardian Turret now starts when the turret is destroyed, not when it is deployed. * Added the ability for players to remotely destroy their Guardian Turret, allowing them to trigger the cooldown if their turret is not nearby. This is done by equipping the Specialization again and holding an interaction for a brief duration. |- |1.5.5 || * Decreased health to 280 from 300 |}

items.descZh: 持续发射纳米医疗光束，为队友快速恢复生命值。
items.imageFile: Mov_m_healinggeam.gif }}  == Usage ==  The Healing Beam can be selected as the specialization gadget of any Medium build loadout. The gadget (together with the Defibrillator) is specifically unavailable in Terminal Attack matches.  The gadget can be held like a weapon. To activate it, the user must be aiming at a teammate. Holding the primary trigger will heal them over time. If the opponent leaves gadget's range or the user's line of sight (such as by going behind a wall) for too long, the Healing Beam disconnects from them.  === Charge-Based Cooldown === The Healing Beam has a battery charge indicated on the gadget as a cross shape that fills up as it is used. While the Healing Beam is not active, this charge reduces over time. If the display fills up completely, the gadget malfunctions and needs to cool down before healing again.   == Stats == === Effects === The Healing Beam can be used by aiming it at another contestant on the user's team within its 13m range and sustaining fire on them. The teammate will be healed at a rate of 46 health per second. The Healing Beam will overheat after healing 253 HP without pause.  === Overheat === When not overheated, pausing for 0.5 seconds will gradually restore total energy at a rate of 40 health points per second.  The Healing Beam has a maximum overheat time of 5.5 seconds. This means that if you continuously heal a teammate (who isn't at full health), the beam will overheat after 5.5 seconds of use, regardless of the healing rate.After overheating, it takes 7.5 seconds to be usable again.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be activated while targeting a teammate. The teammate needs to remain within line of sight to continue healing them.   Uses up charge while used. Recharges over time. The Healing Beam can overheat if used to its limit, causing it to go on a cooldown.   Forces the user to stop using their other items for an extended time to be able to use the gadget effectively.   Cannot be used to heal the user.  ==== Heal Beam ====  Applies a positive effect to teammates.   Can not be removed by the APS Turret.   Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage.  == Guide == === Strengths === * The more health the user's teammates have, the more effective the Healing Beam will be. A team with at least one Heavy provides a lot of value for the Healing Beam. * The Healing Beam is effective while defending objectives in the open, such as the platform on Power Shift.  === Weaknesses === * The wielder is defenseless while using the Healing Beam and cannot retaliate. A way of countering strategies that involve the Healing Beam is to focus the Healing Beam user.    == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!<center>Changes</center> |- |8.0.0 || *Increased healing rate from 40 per second to 46 per second |- |7.6.0 || *VFX now use team colors, making it easier to tell who is healing who |- |5.8.0 || *Added a sound to indicate the target is completely healed |- |4.6.0 || *Decreased max target distance from 12m to 10m *Decreased max healing distance from 15m to 13m *Decreased time before we disconnect a blocked healing beam, from 1s to 0.75s |- |4.0.0 || * Decreased healing rate from 50 health per second to 40 health per second |- |3.6.0 || * Decreased the time taken until the Healing Beam can overheat from 7s to 5.5s |} Category:Healing Sources

items.description: Throw an orb that creates a shockwave on impact, knocking opponents and objects away from the blast.
items.descZh: 释放高能震荡波，强力击退敌人并打乱阵型。
items.imageFile: Mov_m_shockwave.gif }} == Usage ==  The Shockwave can be selected as the specialization gadget of any Medium build loadout.   When the Specialization key is tapped, the user will summon a Shockwave in their left hand and then proceed to launch it forwards at where their crosshair is placed.   When the Specialization key is held, the user will still summon a Shockwave, however will continue holding it until releasing the Specialization key or being interrupted. Holding the Specialization key does not increase the radius or the strength of the Shockwave, however releasing a held Shockwave is slightly faster than summoning then launching a Shockwave.    == Stats == === Effects === The Shockwave projectile will explode on impact of any surface, and when it does it will release an equal amount of force from the point of impact within it's entire radius, knocking away the user, opponents, Arena Carriables, the Cashout Station, and detach Sticky Gadgets before also knocking them away. The Shockwave will ignore teammates.   The Shockwave will also do minor amounts of environmental damage, enough to break glass and windows.   The Shockwave also disrupts opponents, forcing them to drop any Arena Carriables they were holding, and knock them off Ziplines and Ladders. The Shockwave does not directly interrupt opponents from held interactions such as revivng and stealing Cashout Stations; however, the knockback from the Shockwave will often create enough distance between opponents and the object they are interacting that it still works to interrupt the interaction.   === Properties === ==== Specialization ====  Strikes targets by aiming and firing at them from a distance.   Keeps a stable accuracy, even while moving and going airborne.   Can be used 2 times. When a charge is used, it automatically recharges over the cooldown time.   Does not stop the user from using their other items while the gadget is active.  ==== Orb ====  Has a travel time. Is not affected by gravity.   Can fly for any amount of time and triggers when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant.   Deals minor structural damage, enough to break windows and glass.    Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage, only pushes them.   Can affect user, but not their teammates.  == Guide == === Strengths === * The Shockwave gives the medium much higher mobility, allowing users to more easily rollout or escape danger.  * The Shockwave's knockback can be used for a variety of purposes, such as knocking away opponents stealing a cashout or off a cliff, knocking a cash box out of an opponent's hand, or knocking a teammate's statue towards the user.  === Weaknesses === * Unlike other Medium specializations, the Shockwave does not provide much teamwide utility like the Dematerializer or the Healing Beam.  * The Shockwave struggles indoors as low ceilings and walls limit the mobility of Shockwave users.  === Tactics === * Launch a Shockwave right before stepping on a Jump Pad or Triangle Pad to combine the push force of both and achieve greater vertical height.  * Landing a Shockwave so that it cancels an opponent's horizontal velocity will knock up opponents. This tactic is called juggling and can be used to close the distance between the Shockwave user and their opponents, which is especially useful for melee weapons such as the Riot Shield.   ==History== {| class="wikitable" !Patch!!<center>Changes</center> |- |10.6.0|| *Reverted a change made in 10.3 that constrained how high players could be launched when combining the Shockwave with the Jump Pad |- |10.0.0|| * Added the Shockwave Specialization to the Medium archetype |- |}  Category:Medium Build Category:Specialization

The goo can be damaged by opponents and teammates to destroy it. The created goo is also highly flammable; a nearby fire will quickly spread to any connected pieces of goo and destroy it after a few seconds. Cannot be destroyed by receiving damage such as from bullets or explosions.  ==== Goo ====  Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. The specialization trigger can be used to toggle the gadget on or off. The shield will remain active as long as it has energy remaining or until it is toggled off. While the Mesh Shield is active, the user can freely move, jump, use ziplines, and so on, but they cannot attack or use other items.   == Stats == === Effects === The Mesh Shield is an energy-based shield that can be deployed to create a protective barrier attached to its user. If the user moves or rotates, the shield moves with them.  The Mesh Shield absorbs incoming attacks (including melee attacks) and deflects projectiles, similarly to the Dome Shield. === Energy-Based Cooldown === The Mesh Shield has 750 total energy. It loses energy when taking damage, and 225 energy is lost each time the player lowers the shield. Energy regenerates only when the shield hasn't taken damage for a short time. There is no cooldown; instead, players must manage the shield's energy, ensuring they don't run out at critical moments. When the shield is destroyed, it needs 300 energy to be deployed again.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be activated to apply an effect to the contestant that used it.   Can be enabled and disabled by reactivating.   Uses up charge while used. Recharges over time. The Mesh Shield stores health as its charge.   Forces the user to stop using their other items for an extended time to be able to use the gadget effectively.  ==== Shield ====  Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it. Cannot be damaged by teammates.   Does not disappear by itself as long as it is not broken.   Absorbs damage from enemy bullets, deflects projectiles, blocks explosions, and stops the Winch Claw.   Contestants can pass through.  == Guide == === Strengths === * The large health pool and general operation of the Mesh Shield allows it to be effective in various offensive and defensive ways. ** Offensively, the shield can be used to push across open spaces that lack cover, cover a team's advance into an already guarded space, or even as a distraction tool. Deploying the shield during combat may cause enemies to become focused on it, allowing your teammates to take advantage. ** Defensively, the Mesh Shield is great at blocking incoming weapon fire, which makes it inherently effective at protecting your teammates who are stealing a Cashout. The shield can also block some thrown gadgets, such as Frag Grenades, which will bounce off of the shield's surface. ** It also blocks the Winch Claw, preventing enemies from displacing the Cashout Station or a teammate who may be trying to steal it. ** Can provide cover to teammates using the M134 Minigun, who are usually vulnerable during the weapon's spin up period. ** Like the Dome Shield, it only blocks enemy projectiles, meaning that teammates can shoot opponents while behind the shield.  === Weaknesses === * The Mesh Shield is directly countered by Glitch effects, such as the ones created by Glitch Barrels or incoming Glitch Grenades. Glitch Grenades in particular will detonate on contact with the shield, instantly closing it. * Closing the shield will place it on cooldown, with a slightly longer cooldown being imposed if the shield was damaged. This prevents contestants from rapidly flickering the shield on and off. * Contestants currently deploying the Mesh Shield can not use their weapon or other gadgets. Switching to another item will close the shield.    ==History== {| class="wikitable" !Patch!!<center>Changes</center> |- |9.0.0|| * Increased max health from 750 to 850 * Added the ability for Mesh Shields to block the Winch Claw |- |5.0.0|| *Reworked the Mesh Shield to make it energy based. items.imageFile: mov_l_gateway.gif }}  == Usage == The Gateway can be selected as one of three gadgets of any Light build loadout.  Holding the primary trigger will prepare a high-velocity overhand throw. Holding the secondary trigger will prepare a low-velocity underhand throw. While preparing a throw, the gadget's trajectory is indicated up to the point where it bounces off a surface (or up to its mid-air detonation point). Swapping to a different item will cancel the throw. Releasing the trigger throws the gadget.   Throwing a second gateway will connect it to the first. To enter a gateway, any contestant can interact with one of the gateways to travel to the other. Alternatively, projectiles and objects can be thrown into the gateway to teleport them on their own.  == Stats == === Effects === The Gateway can be deployed by throwing it. A few seconds after being deployed, it creates a closed gateway. The same process is repeated for the second deployment, at which point the two gateways connect. Contestants (including opponents) can use the gateway to travel to the other gateway (with a cooldown of 3 seconds) until it disappears after 20 seconds. Additionally, any objects (such as the Frag Grenade or a barrel) are also teleported if they come into a gateway's proximity.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be thrown like a grenade, meaning overhand or underhand. The trajectory and explosion point are shown as an indicator.   Has 2 charges, but both need to be used to create a gateway. Recharging starts when both charges are used and restores both charges at once.  ==== Projectile ====  Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time.   Bounces away when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant.   Triggers after a fixed amount of time, regardless of whether the projectile has struck opponents or surfaces.   Can be removed by the APS Turret, nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health.   Can be reshaped by the Data Reshaper into a piece of decor by opponents.  ==== Gateway ====  Can be temporarily disabled by a Glitch Grenade or Glitch Barrel.   Can be used by opponents to their advantage.   Provides a special mode of transport for contestants. Also teleports projectiles and objects that go near the gateway.   Can be reshaped by the Data Reshaper, closing both ends of the gateway.   Does not attach to a surface upon deployment.   Cannot be destroyed by receiving damage such as from bullets or explosions.  == Guide == === Strengths === * A gateway can be held unopened for as long as needed. The duration begins only when the second gateway is placed.  === Weaknesses === * Opponents can follow the user through their gateway.  === Tactics === * A gateway can be made to detonate in mid-air, so that it becomes a one-way portal as contestants would not be able to reach it. * By activating a gateway with one portal on a vault, the cash box from said vault can automatically be teleported as soon as the vault unlocks. This is often useful to bypass teams that might be contesting the vault or to gain a tempo advantage by quickly activating a cashout station. * An inactive portal is deployed indefinitely as long as the user stays within its 50m range. Hence a portal can be placed down before entering a fight, and returned to very quickly by deploying the second portal and entering the gateway. This trick can be used to get out of sticky situations or to quickly change position and surprise an enemy. * A gateway can be used to quickly reposition an entire team, whether that be to a strategic position or simply out of a sticky situation. * Mines, barrels, and other projectiles such as RPGs can be transported through the gateway, letting contestants eliminate opponents remotely.       == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!<center>Changes</center> |- |9.0.0 || * Decreased max range from 70m to 50m |- |5.0.0 || * Gateways will now destroy surrounding goo when activated |- |2.2.0 || * Fixed an issue that allowed gateways to deploy without enough clearance above them * Fixed an issue where there was no distance limit for the gateway gadget |- |2.0.0 || * Gateway was introduced into the game |- |}

A few seconds after being deployed, it starts emitting pulses that scan a large spherical area around the gadget. The pulses travel through surfaces. Any opponent in its radius the moment a pulse begins will have their location revealed to the user's team for a few moments.  The user's team can see the opponent in the form of particles in the shape of their body in the color of their team, which are visible regardless of distance or any surfaces between the target and the viewer. The target has a warning on their screen that they are detected. === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be thrown like a grenade, meaning overhand or underhand. The trajectory and explosion point are shown as an indicator.   Can be used 2 times. items.description: When charged, can be used on fallen teammates' statues to revive them instantly

items.imageFile: mov_m_defibrillator.gif }}  == Usage == The Defibrillator can be selected as one of three gadgets of any Medium build loadout, except when competing in the Terminal Attack and Team Deathmatch gamemodes.  Once equipped, holding the primary fire button will prepare an activation of the Defibrillator. Releasing the button will activate the gadget as long as a valid target is within range and the minimum charge duration of 1 second is met.  == Stats == === Effects === The Defibrillator, once deployed, must be prepared for a brief moment before activation. The contestant using the gadget is required to be both facing and within a short distance of either a teammate's Revive Statue or an opposing contestant.  When a Defibrillator is used on a Revive Statue, it starts an uninterruptible revival process that requires no further action from the user. A hologram appears at the statue's location and gradually re-materializes during the revival. Once the process is complete: *The revived contestant returns with half of their Build's maximum HP. Light 75, Medium 125, Heavy 175. *They gain brief invulnerability. *They suffer temporary revive sickness, which prevents them from using their Specializations or Gadgets for 5 seconds after being revived.  Alternatively, the Defibrillator can be activated on an opposing contestant to instantly deal 50 damage to them.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be activated while targeting a Revive Statue to revive it (or alternatively, an opponent to damage them).   Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time.  ==== Zap ====  Can be used on an opponent to deal some damage to them.   Can not be removed by the APS Turret.  ==== Effect ====  Applies a positive effect to teammates.   Cannot be disabled by a Glitch Grenade or Glitch Barrel, meaning the revive in progress will not be interrupted.   Cannot be reshaped by the Data Reshaper.  == Guide == === Strengths === * The Defibrillator can revive teammates faster and without needing to do so manually past the initial activation. ** This allows contestants to fight, defend or assist with objectives while the revive is in progress, instead of remaining still for multiple seconds to perform a full revive.  === Weaknesses === * Contestants revived by the Defibrillator are left at a disadvantage, with 50% their maximum HP and being unable to use Specializations or Gadgets for 5 seconds. *Opposing contestants can easily camp and kill a teammate being revived by the Defibrillator due to the obvious hologram, timing, and sound cues. The defibrillator revive also becomes a waste if both the user and their revived teammate die during and/or immediately after the revival. ** To prevent this, contestants who are reviving a teammate should try to remain in close proximity to them. This will allow the contestant performing the revive to try and protect them from enemy contestants. Alternatively, the Revive Statue can be moved to a safer location before using the Defibrillator. *Using the Defibrillator as a weapon is highly impractical. Not only is it slower and deals slightly less damage than a melee attack, the Defibrillator's cooldown is incurred once it damages an enemy, effectively wasting it.  ===Tactics=== * It is the responsibility of the Defibrillator user to ensure that their teammate won't immediately die upon revival. Moving the teammate's Revive Statue away from enemies or providing cover with abilities such as Goo, the APS Turret, or the Guardian Turret can all but guarantee the odds of successful revives. * The Defibrillator is best used for mid-fight Revives, such as if a teammate dies early into a fight. * The Healing Beam makes an excellent pairing with the Defibrillator, as it can heal the revived contestant and make them battle-ready quicker.     == Trivia == All but one contestant eliminated on The Boundless. This would be a perfect time to have equipped a defibrillator!|source=Scotty  == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!<center>Changes</center> |- |7.6.0 || *Increased charge time from 0.8s to 1s  |- |5.8.0 || *Fixed an issue that allowed players to vault while being revived by Defibrillator |- |5.0.0 || *Added ‘revive sickness’ to players revived by the Defibrillator, causing their Specializations and Gadgets to be placed on a five-second cooldown |- |4.0.0 || *Fixed an issue where the lobby screen only showed Defibrillators on all icons when first entering the screen |- |3.12.0 || * Fixed a bug where defibrillation revive got blocked by friendly Mesh and Dome shields |- |2.7.0 || *Fixed an issue where Guardian Turrets would target respawning Defibrillated players who are immune to damage |- |2.0.0 || *Added functionality that causes revived players to gradually re-materialize into the level over a period of 3s before fully loading back into the arena *Increased charge-up time from 0.6s to 0.8s *Increased starting health from a defibrillator revive from 40% to 50% |- |1.6.0 || *Fixed an issue where player statues could not be targeted for revives when lying in foliage *Fixed an issue where player statues could not be targeted for revives when carried |- |1.5.5 || * Decreased the length of invulnerability applied after a revive to 0.75s from 1.5s |- |1.2.0 || *Added ability for defibrillators to damage enemy players. They will do 50 damage and will enter cooldown if they land a successful hit |}

While the gadget is held, an indicator will show a potential placement of the Hover Pad as a blue hologram in front of the user. If the hologram is red, the gadget will not fit in the target location. Using the primary trigger, the placement can be confirmed to deploy the gadget. It can be deployed only in the air.  The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.  == Stats ==  === Effects === The pad can be pushed and moved in the air by explosives, Shockwaves, and most noticeably Powder Canisters.    === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be placed anywhere in the air, but cannot attach to things. It will not attach directly to ceilings despite the indicator being blue.   Can be placed once, its cooldown will not recharge until it is retrieved or destroyed.   Can be picked up by interacting with the pad, refunding about half a cooldown.   Can be commanded to self destruct from any distance, refunding about half a cooldown.  ==== Pad ====  Has its own collision, meaning it blocks bullets, contestants can stand on it, and other gadgets can be attached to it.   Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions.   When glitched by enemies the hover pad will instantly fall, and breaks upon hitting the ground.  == Guide == === Strengths ===   === Weaknesses === * The pad will be weighed down considerably by any Cashout Stations, quickly hitting the ground if holding one up. * If any Arena Carriables are dropped onto the pad, it will deal damage to the pad.  === Tactics === * If the Hover Pad is broken by an explosion, any attached gadget (that isn't also broken in the explosion) will be sent flying in the opposite direction. * If there is a sniper above you while stealing a Cashout Station, placing the pad above you like a vertical shield is an effective strategy. * Unlike the Guardian Turret, Retrieving the Hover Pad remotely has the same cooldown time as picking it up manually.     == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!<center>Changes</center> |- |11.0.0 || *Increased health from 350 to 425 |- |10.3.0 || *Increased health from 300 to 350 |- |10.0.0 || * Added the Hover Pad Gadget to the Medium archetype |- |}

While the gadget is held, an indicator will show a potential placement of the Jump Pad as a blue hologram in front of the user. If the hologram is red, the gadget will not fit in the target location. Using the primary trigger, the placement can be confirmed to deploy the gadget. It can be deployed on any surface, including walls and ceilings.  The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.  == Stats == === Effects === The Jump Pad can be deployed by placing it on any nearby surface. Any contestants or objects that touch the active part of the Jump Pad will be launched. Opponents and teammates alike can damage the Jump Pad to destroy it.  The gadget can be placed in any orientation. It will always launch objects in the orientation it is facing. For example, a Jump Pad placed on a wall will push objects away from the wall.  The cashout station, barrels, cash boxes, and the Frag Grenade are all examples of objects that can be affected by the Jump Pad.  The Jump Pad is usually placed either on a floor to launch straight up, or on a sloped surface. A sloped Jump Pad will launch contestants far across the arena.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be placed attached to a surface. An indicator shows the exact target placement.   Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time.   Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge.   One Jump Pad can be deployed at a time. A new deployment causes the existing Jump Pad to disappear.  ==== Pad ====  Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any carriable object it is attached to.   Has its own collision, meaning it blocks bullets and contestants can stand on it.   Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it.   Can be reshaped by the Data Reshaper into a piece of decor by opponents.   Can be used by opponents to their advantage.   Provides a special mode of transport for contestants. Also causes projectiles and objects to bounce.   Starts working immediately upon deployment.   Cannot be disabled by a Glitch Grenade or Glitch Barrel.   Disappears by itself after enough time has passed.  == Guide == === Strengths === * When placed on a slope at an angle, such as on a roof in Monaco, the user can travel a very far horizontal distance. The distance travelled becomes extreme during the Low Gravity event.  === Weaknesses === * The Jump Pad can be destroyed by nearby damage from any source. However, it has a lot of health compared to most gadgets. * Poor placement of the Jump Pad can cause teammates to waste time and leave them out of position. * There is a small amount of variance to the Jump Pad's launch angle, preventing objects from bouncing on them indefinitely.  === Tactics === * Thrown gadgets, as well as the projectiles from the CL-40 can be bounced off of a Jump Pad, which can be useful for shooting around a cover such as by placing it on the wall in a doorway. However, placing the Jump Pad can only be done from a short distance making it effective only as a defensive tool. * Sprinting, sliding or dashing into a jump pad will give the user additional horizontal distance. * Can be placed on top of Goo to create an angled launch.     == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!<center>Changes</center> |- |5.0.0 || * Increased cooldown from 30s to 40s |- |4.0.0 || * Added a small amount of variance to the Jump Pad so that objects cannot bounce on them indefinitely |- |2.0.0 || * Increased cooldown from 25s to 30s |- |CB1 Balance Patch 1 || * Reduced the number of Jump Pads players can have deployed at once from 2 to 1. * Jump pad cooldown reduced from 20 seconds to 15 seconds. |- |}

items.name: Anti-Gravity Cube
items.description: Deployable that manipulates gravity in its immediate area, lifting contestants and objects upwards
items.descZh: 生成立方体失重区域，使提现机、废墟与敌人全部漂浮至空中。
items.imageFile: mov_h_antigravity.gif}}  == Usage == The Anti-Gravity Cube can be selected as one of three gadgets of any Heavy build loadout.  Holding the primary trigger will prepare a high-velocity overhand throw. Holding the secondary trigger will prepare a low-velocity underhand throw. While preparing a throw, the gadget's trajectory is indicated up to the point where it triggers on impact. Releasing the trigger will execute the throw, whereas swapping to a different item will cancel it.  == Stats == === Effects === The Anti-Gravity Cube can be thrown, and when it hits the ground, it creates a large cylindrical area (8 meters in diameter and 12 meters tall) that rises upwards from the gadget. This area moves along with the cube and can pass through surfaces.  Contestants and objects inside this area will levitate and slowly rise upwards until they reach the maximum height of the gadget's range. Even the Cashout Station can be lifted and moved by this effect.  === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be thrown like a grenade, meaning overhand or underhand. The trajectory and impact point are shown as an indicator.   Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time.   Cannot be picked up after being deployed.  ==== Projectile ====  Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time.   Bounces away when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant.   Can fly for any amount of time and triggers when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant.   Can be removed by the APS Turret, nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health.   Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it.   Can be reshaped by the Data Reshaper into a piece of decor by opponents.   Produces a sound whenever it teleports something, alerting nearby contestants.   Can be used by opponents to their advantage.   Provides a special mode of transport for contestants. Also works for moving projectiles and objects.   Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage.   Cannot be disabled by a Glitch Grenade or Glitch Barrel.   Does not inflict damage.  == Guide == === Strengths === * The Anti-Gravity Cube can lift the Cashout Station, making it easier to defend - or in some situations, easier to steal. * The Anti-Gravity Cube can slow down players that enter it's radius without significant momentum and make them easy-to-hit, floating targets. * The Anti-Gravity Cube's effect area can pass and affect targets through surfaces above the cube in range. * The Anti-Gravity Cube's effect area, although being a slow ascend, can help contestants reach elevated places.  === Weaknesses === * The Anti-Gravity Cube does not have shielding, destructive or damaging properties compared to the majority of the Heavy archetype's other options. * The Strength of being able to make enemies easy-to-hit, floating targets can also apply to the contestant using it and their teammates themselves, should they misplace it. * The Anti-Gravity Cube only has 150 HP and so can be very quickly destroyed with majority of Weapons. It can also be reshaped by the Data Reshaper and destroyed by an APS Turret.  * With the radius being only 4 meters wide, the active area is not particularly big, making inaccurate throws combined with the 28s cooldown quite punishing.  === Tactics === * During offense, the Anti-Gravity Cube can lift a Cashout Station that is being defended by an enemy team from above which allows the contestant's team to maintain the height advantage, rather than having to push into the area from the same height or below it. ** C4, the RPG-7, Explosive Canisters and especially the KS-23 with it's ability to damage and destroy the enviroment by simply shooting are great to utilise with the cube in order to create openings above the Cashout Station, should it be in an enclosed area. * During defense preparation, the Anti-Gravity Cube can be used to lift the Cashout Station prematurely to put it into advantegous positions. For instance, together with Goo from a Goo Barrel, Goo Grenade or Goo Gun, it can be fixated at the ceiling of a room, preventing common tactics of safely dropping the station from a floor below. With enough Goo, the Station could be fully encased in this elevated positon, making it even more difficult to reach quickly. * During active defense, the Anti-Gravity Cube can be used to great extent to stall steals. ** While an enemy contestant could continue stealing the Cashout Station while they're both being lifted, they will be in an even more helpless position as they won't be able to escape easily while continuously floating. ** Depending on the positions, the Cashout Station could continue to float up while the enemy contestant stealing gets stopped by parts of the ceiling and vice versa, breaking line of sight and stopping a steal. ** The Anti-Gravity Cube can be destroyed on purpose to make floating players and the cashout fall unexpectedly, potentially making the stealing contestant cancel their interaction. * When in an open area or with enough space, the Anti-Gravity Cube can be thrown behind enemy Barricades and walls of Goo, lifting enemy contestants in range out of their defenses, forcing them to be slow and exposed or reposition. * The effect area of the Anti-Gravity Cube can trap players in the ceilings of rooms if theyre caught on map geometry or other objects, forcing them to destroy the cube to get down or make use of certain Specializations or Gadgets. ** This can be utilised when being chased and is particularly effective against enemies with melee weapons. The contestant can throw the cube behind them in hallways or other enclosed areas with tight access like doorframes, windows and vents. The user's team can see the opponent in the form of particles in the shape of their body in the color of their team, which are visible regardless of distance or any surfaces between the target and the viewer.   The target has a warning on their screen that they are detected, and a visual effect shows a line from the target to the gadget to let them know where it is. === Properties === ==== Gadget ====  Can be thrown out a short distance, after which it attaches to the first surface it hits.
